Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 91, verses 1–10:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-duha (وضحاها): i.e., and its daylight.

Idha talaha (إذا تلاها): i.e., when it follows the sun, rising immediately after its setting, and that is on the night of the middle of the month.

Idha jallaha (إذا جلاها): i.e., when it illuminates it.

Idha yaghshaha (إذا يغشاها): i.e., when it covers the sun until the horizons become dark.

Wa-ma banaha (وما بناها): i.e., and He who built it, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Who made the sky like a roof for the earth.

Wa-ma tahaha (وما طحاها): i.e., and He who spread it out, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Wa-ma sawwaha (وما سواها): i.e., and He who fashioned its creation and balanced it, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Fa-alhamaha fujuraha (فألهمها فجورها): i.e., He made clear to it what it should do or abandon of good and evil.

Aflaha man zakkaha (أفلح من زكاها): i.e., he succeeds in attaining salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise, the one who purifies his soul from sins and wrongdoings.

Wa-qad khaba (وقد خاب): i.e., he loses in the Hereafter, himself and his family on the Day of Resurrection.

Man dassaha (من دساها): i.e., he buries his soul when he conceals and degrades it with disbelief and disobedience. The root of dassaha is dassasa, and one of the two sin letters was changed to a ya'.

Meaning of the verses:

The verses from His saying ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ to His saying ﴿and he has failed who buries it﴾ contain ten verses comprising a divine oath of the greatest oaths, the thing sworn upon, which is the answer to the oath, and the ones addressed, who are all of mankind. The oath is by the following: by the sun and its brightness; by the moon when it follows it, i.e., rises after its setting, and that is on the night of the middle of the month; by the day when it reveals it, i.e., when it illuminates, dispelling darkness, or the world; by the night when it covers it, i.e., covers the sun until the horizons become dark; by the sky and He who built it, though the term "ma" is generally used for non-rational beings, it can also refer to rational beings, as it does here. He who built it is Allah, glorified and exalted, and by the earth and He who spread it out, i.e., spread it, and He is Allah, the Exalted; and by the soul and He who fashioned it, i.e., created it and balanced its creation, and He is Allah, the Exalted. His saying ﴿and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ means He created it, fashioned its creation, and inspired it, i.e., made clear to it good and evil: what it should do of righteous deeds and what it should avoid of corrupting acts. Thus Allah, the Exalted, swore by four of His great creations and by Himself, the Most High, the Mighty, upon what is indicated by His saying ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who buries it﴾. This is the thing sworn upon: that whoever Allah grants success and assists, so that he purifies his soul, i.e., cleanses it through faith and righteous deeds, keeping it distant from what defiles it of polytheism and disobedience, he has succeeded, meaning he wins on the Day of Resurrection by being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise, because the linguistic meaning of success is safety from what is feared and attainment of what is desired. And whoever Allah forsakes, because of his previous history in evil and corruption, so that he does not purify his soul with faith and righteous deeds, and buries it, i.e., conceals and degrades it with the sins poured over it and the traces of wrongdoing and transgressions covering it, he has lost, meaning he has lost in his Hereafter, and so he has not succeeded; he has lost himself and his family, and that is the manifest loss.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Demonstration of the manifestations of divine power in the verses by which the Lord, the Exalted, swore.

2- Explanation of what success is achieved by, and what loss results from.

3- Encouragement toward faith and righteous deeds, and warning against polytheism and disobedience.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 91, verses 1–10:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-duha (وضحاها): i.e., and its daylight.

Idha talaha (إذا تلاها): i.e., when it follows the sun, rising immediately after its setting, and that is on the night of the middle of the month.

Idha jallaha (إذا جلاها): i.e., when it illuminates it.

Idha yaghshaha (إذا يغشاها): i.e., when it covers the sun until the horizons become dark.

Wa-ma banaha (وما بناها): i.e., and He who built it, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Who made the sky like a roof for the earth.

Wa-ma tahaha (وما طحاها): i.e., and He who spread it out, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Wa-ma sawwaha (وما سواها): i.e., and He who fashioned its creation and balanced it, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Fa-alhamaha fujuraha (فألهمها فجورها): i.e., He made clear to it what it should do or abandon of good and evil.

Aflaha man zakkaha (أفلح من زكاها): i.e., he succeeds in attaining salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise, the one who purifies his soul from sins and wrongdoings.

Wa-qad khaba (وقد خاب): i.e., he loses in the Hereafter, himself and his family on the Day of Resurrection.

Man dassaha (من دساها): i.e., he buries his soul when he conceals and degrades it with disbelief and disobedience. The root of dassaha is dassasa, and one of the two sin letters was changed to a ya'.

Meaning of the verses:

The verses from His saying ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ to His saying ﴿and he has failed who buries it﴾ contain ten verses comprising a divine oath of the greatest oaths, the thing sworn upon, which is the answer to the oath, and the ones addressed, who are all of mankind. The oath is by the following: by the sun and its brightness; by the moon when it follows it, i.e., rises after its setting, and that is on the night of the middle of the month; by the day when it reveals it, i.e., when it illuminates, dispelling darkness, or the world; by the night when it covers it, i.e., covers the sun until the horizons become dark; by the sky and He who built it, though the term "ma" is generally used for non-rational beings, it can also refer to rational beings, as it does here. He who built it is Allah, glorified and exalted, and by the earth and He who spread it out, i.e., spread it, and He is Allah, the Exalted; and by the soul and He who fashioned it, i.e., created it and balanced its creation, and He is Allah, the Exalted. His saying ﴿and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ means He created it, fashioned its creation, and inspired it, i.e., made clear to it good and evil: what it should do of righteous deeds and what it should avoid of corrupting acts. Thus Allah, the Exalted, swore by four of His great creations and by Himself, the Most High, the Mighty, upon what is indicated by His saying ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who buries it﴾. This is the thing sworn upon: that whoever Allah grants success and assists, so that he purifies his soul, i.e., cleanses it through faith and righteous deeds, keeping it distant from what defiles it of polytheism and disobedience, he has succeeded, meaning he wins on the Day of Resurrection by being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise, because the linguistic meaning of success is safety from what is feared and attainment of what is desired. And whoever Allah forsakes, because of his previous history in evil and corruption, so that he does not purify his soul with faith and righteous deeds, and buries it, i.e., conceals and degrades it with the sins poured over it and the traces of wrongdoing and transgressions covering it, he has lost, meaning he has lost in his Hereafter, and so he has not succeeded; he has lost himself and his family, and that is the manifest loss.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 91, verses 11–15:

Explanation of the words:

Thamud: that is, the People of the Rock (Ashab al-Hijr), who denied their messenger Salih, peace be upon him.

Bi-taghwaha: that is, because of their transgression in shirk and sins.

Idhi-ntba'atha: that is, he set off hastily.

Ashqaha: that is, the most wretched of the tribe, who was Qudar ibn Salif, and by whom a proverb is made, so it is said, "More ill-omened than Qudar."

Rasul Allah: that is, Salih, peace be upon him.

Naqata Allah wa-suqyaha: that is, leave her and her drink on her day.

Fa-kadhdhabuhu: that is, regarding what he told them about the she-camel.

Fa-'aqaruha: that is, they killed her so that the water of her drink on her day would be cleared for them.

Fa-damdama: that is, the punishment closed in upon them and destroyed them.

Bi-dhanbihim: that is, because of their sins, which were shirk, denial, and the killing of the she-camel.

Fa-sawwaha: that is, He levelled the destruction over them, so not one of them escaped.

Wa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha: that is, the Lord, exalted is He, does not fear the consequence of their destruction as a person fears the outcome of his action when he kills someone or punishes him.

Meaning of the verses:

His statement, exalted is He, ﴿Thamud denied﴾ through to His statement ﴿and He does not fear its consequence﴾: these verses were brought to demonstrate matters, namely that sins necessitate the punishment of God in this world and the next; that the denial of the Messenger, in which the Meccan disbelievers persist, is a warning of great danger if they continue in it, for God may destroy them by it as He destroyed the People of the Rock, the people of Salih; that Muhammad is truly and certainly the Messenger of God, and that the Quraysh's denial of him has no worth; and that there is no god but God. And that resurrection and recompense are established by the proofs of God's power and knowledge. So His statement, exalted is He, ﴿Thamud denied﴾ is an report from Him, exalted is He, whose purpose is to warn the Quraysh of the danger of persisting in denial, and to console the Messenger and the believers. His statement ﴿because of their transgression﴾ means because of their sins, which reached the limit of transgression, which is excess and exceeding the bounds in the matter. God, exalted is He, specified the time of that by His statement ﴿when there set off﴾ the most wretched of that tribe, who was Qudar ibn Salif, by whom a proverb is made regarding wretchedness, so it is said, "More ill-omened than Qudar." The Messenger of God said of him, "The most wretched of the first and the last is Qudar ibn Salif." His statement: the Messenger of God, that is Salih, said to them ﴿the she-camel of God﴾, that is, beware of her; so leave her to eat in the land of God, and do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment seize you. ﴿Leave her and her drink﴾, that is, the water of her drinking, since the water was divided between them and her: a day for her and a day for them. ﴿But they denied him﴾ in that and in other matters of his message and his call to worship God alone. ﴿So they hamstrung her﴾, that is, they slaughtered her. ﴿Then their Lord levelled over them﴾, that is, the punishment closed in upon them and enveloped them, so none of them was spared; and that was because of their sin, not by any injustice from Him, exalted is He. ﴿And He levelled it﴾ in vengeance and punishment. ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾, that is, no consequence reaches Him from their destruction, for He is the Lord of all and the Owner of all, the Subduer above His servants, the Mighty, the Wise.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that the servant's salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise depends on purifying his soul and cleansing it of the filth of sins and disobedience, and that the servant's wretchedness and loss is caused by his defiling his soul with shirk and sins; all of this is among the laws of God, exalted is He, regarding causes and their effects.

2- A warning against transgression, which is excess in evil and corruption, for it is destructive and ruinous and necessitates destruction and ruin in this world and punishment in the next.

3- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ and lightening his burden, since before Quraysh, Thamud and other nations denied, such as the People of Madyan, the people of Lot, and Pharaoh.

4- A warning to the Meccan disbelievers of the consequence of shirk, denial, and sins of wrongdoing and aggression.

His statement: the Messenger of God, that is Salih, said to them ﴿the she-camel of God﴾, that is, beware of her; so leave her to eat in the land of God, and do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment seize you. ﴿Leave her and her drink﴾, that is, the water of her drinking, since the water was divided between them and her: a day for her and a day for them. ﴿But they denied him﴾ in that and in other matters of his message and his call to worship God alone. ﴿So they hamstrung her﴾, that is, they slaughtered her. ﴿Then their Lord levelled over them﴾, that is, the punishment closed in upon them and enveloped them, so none of them was spared; and that was because of their sin, not by any injustice from Him, exalted is He. ﴿And He levelled it﴾ in vengeance and punishment. ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾, that is, no consequence reaches Him from their destruction, for He is the Lord of all and the Owner of all, the Subduer above His servants, the Mighty, the Wise.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that the servant's salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise depends on purifying his soul and cleansing it of the filth of sins and disobedience, and that the servant's wretchedness and loss is caused by his defiling his soul with shirk and sins; all of this is among the laws of God, exalted is He, regarding causes and their effects.

2- A warning against transgression, which is excess in evil and corruption, for it is destructive and ruinous and necessitates destruction and ruin in this world and punishment in the next.

3- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ and lightening his burden, since before Quraysh, Thamud and other nations denied, such as the People of Madyan, the people of Lot, and Pharaoh.

4- A warning to the Meccan disbelievers of the consequence of shirk, denial, and sins of wrongdoing and aggression.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 91, verses 11–15:

Explanation of the words:

Thamud: that is, the People of the Rock (Ashab al-Hijr), who denied their messenger Salih, peace be upon him.

Bi-taghwaha: that is, because of their transgression in shirk and sins.

Idhi-ntba'atha: that is, he set off hastily.

Ashqaha: that is, the most wretched of the tribe, who was Qudar ibn Salif, and by whom a proverb is made, so it is said, "More ill-omened than Qudar."

Rasul Allah: that is, Salih, peace be upon him.

Naqata Allah wa-suqyaha: that is, leave her and her drink on her day.

Fa-kadhdhabuhu: that is, regarding what he told them about the she-camel.

Fa-'aqaruha: that is, they killed her so that the water of her drink on her day would be cleared for them.

Fa-damdama: that is, the punishment closed in upon them and destroyed them.

Bi-dhanbihim: that is, because of their sins, which were shirk, denial, and the killing of the she-camel.

Fa-sawwaha: that is, He levelled the destruction over them, so not one of them escaped.

Wa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha: that is, the Lord, exalted is He, does not fear the consequence of their destruction as a person fears the outcome of his action when he kills someone or punishes him.

Meaning of the verses:

His statement, exalted is He, ﴿Thamud denied﴾ through to His statement ﴿and He does not fear its consequence﴾: these verses were brought to demonstrate matters, namely that sins necessitate the punishment of God in this world and the next; that the denial of the Messenger, in which the Meccan disbelievers persist, is a warning of great danger if they continue in it, for God may destroy them by it as He destroyed the People of the Rock, the people of Salih; that Muhammad is truly and certainly the Messenger of God, and that the Quraysh's denial of him has no worth; and that there is no god but God. And that resurrection and recompense are established by the proofs of God's power and knowledge. So His statement, exalted is He, ﴿Thamud denied﴾ is an report from Him, exalted is He, whose purpose is to warn the Quraysh of the danger of persisting in denial, and to console the Messenger and the believers. His statement ﴿because of their transgression﴾ means because of their sins, which reached the limit of transgression, which is excess and exceeding the bounds in the matter.
